drivingQuestion: Does acquiring residence in a town require intention?
outcomeNote: Mishna records the dispute with R' Yehuda's precedent

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁיָּשַׁב בַּדֶּרֶךְ, וְעָמַד וְרָאָה הֲרֵי (זֶה) הוּא סָמוּךְ לָעִיר, [הוֹאִיל] וְלֹא הָיְתָה כַּוּוֹנָתוֹ לְכָךְ — לֹא יִכָּנֵס. דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» With regard to «a person who was sitting along the road» on Shabbat eve toward nightfall, unaware that he was within the city’s Shabbat limit, «and» when «he stood up» after Shabbat had already commenced, «he saw that he was near the town,» i.e., within its limit, «since he had not intended» to acquire his place of residence in the town, «he may not enter» it, but rather he measures two thousand cubits from his place; this is «the statement of Rabbi Meir.»

segments.he: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: יִכָּנֵס. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מַעֲשֶׂה הָיָה וְנִכְנַס רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן בְּלֹא מִתְכַּוֵּין.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda says: He may enter» the town. «Rabbi Yehuda said: It once happened that Rabbi Tarfon entered» a town on Shabbat «without intention» from the beginning of Shabbat to establish residence in the city.

moves.summary: R' Meir: without intention he may not enter
Precedent: R' Tarfon entered without intention

positions.claim: he may not enter, since he did not intend to acquire residence there
